text: You’re deep in focus, absorbed in your task. Your mind is sharp, concentration unwavering. You just want to stay in that productive flow, undisturbed.
Suddenly, a tiny flicker. A notification pops. You feel an irresistible tug. Focus breaks, you reach for your device.
Why does that alert feel urgent? You might assume every notification is crucial, a vital piece you can't miss.
But the real mechanism is intermittent reinforcement. Most notifications are trivial, yet some deliver a true reward. That unpredictability trains you to check every time.
This system has a cost. Your attention fragments, constantly pulled. You pay with lost focus and anxiety, always waiting for that next hit.
Tomorrow, the pings will still come. But now you see the hidden machinery: apps aren't just sending messages; they're training you, hooked on the *chance* of reward.
